scenarios.name: Same workload with two policies
scenarios.setup: 12 tasks, seed 305, burst at t=0, default nodes; fresh engine per policy.
scenarios.expected: Capacity-aware placement may distribute tasks differently. Neither policy exceeds capacity or admits a task above its latency budget.
scenarios.actual: 10/12 placements differ. Lowest-latency completed 12; capacity-aware completed 12.

scenarios.name: Overload and fallback
scenarios.setup: 30 simultaneous medium-sensitivity tasks, each 3 CPU, 6 GiB RAM and 40 ms service; lowest-latency policy.
scenarios.expected: Fill Edge, then fall back to Fog and Cloud. Reject remaining tasks when no suitable capacity remains.
scenarios.actual: 17 completed and 13 rejected. Admitted tasks span 3 tiers.

scenarios.name: Unauthorized tenant access
scenarios.setup: Alice owns PRIVATE-A. Bob owns PRIVATE-B and requests Alice's task, then exports his own records.
scenarios.expected: Deny Bob's direct read and exclude Alice's task and VM from his export.
scenarios.actual: Direct read denied. Bob sees ['PRIVATE-B']. Export isolation=True.

scenarios.name: Capacity and latency change
scenarios.setup: Repeat E1 lowest-latency workload after changing Edge from 8 CPU/16 GiB/5 ms to 16 CPU/32 GiB/2 ms.
scenarios.expected: Larger, faster Edge admits more tasks locally and changes response time and resource utilization.
scenarios.actual: 4/12 placements change. Mean response 69.25 ms before and 59.292 ms after. Fog peak CPU falls from 93.75% to 43.75%; Edge peak CPU remains 100% with twice the capacity.
